newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler sells AEG Electrocom to Siemens.
newsitem.headline: Daimler sells AEG Electrocom to Siemens.

text.p: Germany's largest industrial group, Daimler-Benz AG, said on Monday it was selling two 100 percent subsidiaries to a unit of electronics group Siemens AG.

The units being sold were listed as AEG Electrocom GmbH and AEG ElectroCom International Inc (ECA), Irving, Texas. They will be transferred to Siemens Nuremberg-based automisation unit, effective January 1 this year.
The sale was part of an continuing Daimler effort to trim operations that did not closely fit its new strategy of concentrating on transportation-related industries.
Since the middle of 1995, the industrial group has slashed the number of operating units to 23 from 35.
Daimler did not disclose the price it received for the sale and said the deal still must be approved by regulatory authorities.
Daimler said that AEG Electrocom enjoys a leading position in the global recognition and sorting systems business and that the operation will fit well with Siemen's automated technology business.
AEG Electrocom had sales of 650 million marks in 1995 and sales of more than one billion marks were expected for 1996. About 70 percent of its business comes from the U.S.
